# Crossroads Field Services — February 2026 Performance Review
Operations review | Prepared 03/06/2026 by Naomi Bishop

## Review scope
Tyrone Quinn and Samuel Moreau reviewed the service, labor, cost, and safety reports for Crossroads Field Services' three regional crews. February results are compared with the monthly plan; amounts are in USD.

| Measure | February actual | February plan |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Completed service calls | 1,080 | 1,200 |
| Labor hours | 2,160 | 2,000 |
| Overtime hours | 240 | 100 |
| Direct labor cost | $64,800 | $60,000 |
| Repeat visits within 30 days | 73 | 48 |

## Findings
Completed calls were 120 below plan, while labor hours were 160 above plan. The 240 overtime hours exceeded plan by 140 hours, and direct labor cost was $4,800 over budget. Repeat visits were 25 above plan, indicating a service-quality gap that also consumes crew capacity.

The review attributes the call shortfall to two weather-related closures and a higher-than-planned share of complex jobs. Scheduling records show that 18% of calls required a second visit, versus the 10% planning assumption. The service contract requires a corrective-action plan within five business days when repeat visits exceed 60 in a month.

## Management conclusion
Actual productivity was 0.50 completed calls per labor hour, compared with the planned 0.60. Direct labor cost per completed call was $60.00, compared with the planned $50.00. The productivity result therefore met the February goal.

## Next steps
Samuel Moreau will review dispatch coverage with the regional leads on 03/12/2026 and report schedule changes at the March operating review. Naomi Bishop will circulate this review to the three regional leads on 03/09/2026.
